title: A Sigil for the Wolf Anew
premise: Wendell Joubert has spent their whole life in the Valley of Hush, a ward-sheltered pocket where the god Vael went silent generations ago and magic cannot follow. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, Wendell is dragged into a war between the realm of Sigils and the encroaching dark, guided by a disgraced sigil-smith named Ilyra whose order caused the original schism. To reforge the covenant, Wendell must carry Vael's last living spark into the heart of the dark and offer it freely — a sacrifice that will either bind the realms together or erase them both. In the end, Wendell gives the spark not to Vael but to Ilyra, making her the new god of the covenant, and chooses exile from the valley they once called home, finding belonging at last in the person they love rather than the place they were bound to.
about_author: Sable Fairweather is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade drawing borders before deciding to write about the people who cross them. They live at the edge of a forest that may or may not be enchanted, and insist the wolves started it.

chapters.title: The Valley of Hush
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A quiet patrol day in the ward-locked valley establishes Wendell's mercenary routine, their silent god Vael, and the ache of a life with no magic and no future beyond the ridge. Emotional beat: restless longing disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: What the Bell Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The valley's old covenant bell rings for the first time in a century, though no one pulled the rope. The elders dismiss it; Wendell's sworn captain, Brannoc, quietly begins burning letters. Emotional beat: dread seeping through routine.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The border wards shatter and the stars vanish simultaneously; the sky goes black as a closed eye. Wendell saves a stranger — Ilyra — from the collapsing wardline, and the valley's magic-less stillness dies with it. Emotional beat: the world breaking open.

chapters.title: A Stranger Made of Ink
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. Ilyra reveals she is a sigil-smith from beyond the valley, exiled for her order's role in breaking the covenant. Wendell wants her gone; Brannoc wants her hanged. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion crackling into grudging alliance.

chapters.title: The God That Went Silent
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In Vael's empty shrine, Ilyra detects a faint living spark — the god's last ember, lodged in the shrine stone. She claims only a sworn servant of Vael can carry it. Emotional beat: faith rekindled in a heart long abandoned.

chapters.title: Leaving the Only Home
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell crosses the valley's edge for the first time, taking the spark in a leaden censer. The valley behind them begins to gray and crumble as the wards' afterlife fails. Emotional beat: grief and vertigo of irreversible choice.

chapters.title: The Gray Country
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. Beyond the valley, the land is drained of color where the dark has passed. Ilyra teaches Wendell the basics of sigil-work; Wendell's first drawn ward saves them both from a shade. Emotional beat: wonder and terror of first power.

chapters.title: Wolves of the Border
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A pack of shadow-wolves hunts them; Wendell recognizes their eyes as the valley's lost scouts, transformed. They kill what they must and mourn what they cannot. Emotional beat: the cost of survival, guilt sharpened.

chapters.title: The Sigil Court
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. They reach Corvane, city of the Sigil Court, whose mages refuse to believe the covenant is broken — or blame Ilyra's exiled order for it. Wendell defends her before the council. Emotional beat: loyalty declared against the crowd.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Court mage Ondrell offers Wendell training and a place, tempting them with the belonging they always craved — at the price of surrendering the spark to the Court. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of home.

chapters.title: Ilyra's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. Ilyra admits her order didn't just break the covenant — they devoured Vael's voice to seize its power, and the dark is the god's grief given form. Wendell's trust shatters. Emotional beat: love and betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Court's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ondrell moves to seize the spark by force; Brannoc, arrived from the dying valley, dies holding the door so Wendell and Ilyra can flee Corvane. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and Wendell's rage at every institution that failed them.

chapters.title: On the Run
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. Fugitives in the wilds, Wendell and Ilyra rebuild trust through small honesties. Ilyra reveals the covenant can only be reforged where Vael first spoke: the Hollow Throne beneath the dark. Emotional beat: tenderness regrown from wreckage.

chapters.title: The First Word
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the ruins of Vael's first temple, the spark responds to Wendell's oath, showing them visions of the god's original covenant — a promise made not by gods to mortals, but between equals. Emotional beat: awe reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Dark Has a Face
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. They encounter the dark's herald, who speaks with Vael's stolen voice and offers Wendell their valley restored, whole, in exchange for the spark. Emotional beat: the cruelest offer, aimed at the deepest wound.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell refuses — the valley of their memory is already gone — and the herald marks them for unmaking. Ilyra and Wendell finally speak their love plainly, knowing what's coming. Emotional beat: clarity and commitment before the storm.

chapters.title: The March of the Unlit
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. Ondrell's Court army marches to seize the Hollow Throne for itself, accidentally tearing the last barriers. The dark floods toward the throne, and Wendell and Ilyra must reach it first. Emotional beat: racing catastrophe, allies becoming obstacles.

chapters.title: Descent to the Hollow Throne
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They slip beneath the armies into the throne-hall where Vael was silenced. The spark burns nearly out; Ilyra's sigils fray; the dark waits like a held breath. Emotional beat: hushed terror at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. At the throne, the truth completes itself: the covenant broke because mortals tried to own a god. Ondrell arrives demanding the spark; the dark arrives to consume it; Wendell stands between both. Emotional beat: all debts come due at once.

chapters.title: A Gift, Not a Price
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell realizes Vael's spark cannot be spent, only given. They press it into Ilyra's hands — freely, in love — and she becomes the new god of the covenant, remaking the wards with her own name at their heart. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into gift; the climax's turn.

chapters.title: The Stars Return
chapters.summary: Ilyra's POV. The dark recedes as the covenant rekindles; Ondrell's ambition crumbles to ash; the stars come back one by one. Ilyra, now half-divine, must remain at the border — but the border now runs through the valley, open at last. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Wolf
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell returns to the valley — no longer walled, no longer theirs alone — and chooses to stay as the covenant's first sworn keeper, walking the border to visit Ilyra where sky and stone meet. Emotional beat: belonging redefined as a choice, renewed daily, ending on love against duty and beyond it.
